scenes.title: Fearless concurrency before the binary exists

beats.say: Data races are the nastiest bugs in systems engineering — two threads colliding on the same memory with no lock in sight. Rust eliminates the entire class before your program even compiles. One single rule governs everything: many shared readers, or one exclusive writer, never both at once.

scenes.title: Send, Sync, and locks that own their data

beats.say: Two compiler marker traits police every thread boundary. Send means ownership can cross threads; Sync means shared references can cross safely. A plain String sails straight through. An Rc pointer or an Arc of RefCell shatters against the wall with error E0277.

Wrap your state in Arc of Mutex, and Rust unlocks a signature design: Mutex owns the data inside it. You cannot touch the inner value without locking, and its MutexGuard unlocks automatically when it drops — even during a panic.

scenes.title: Scoped threads, atomics, and bounded channels

beats.say: Ordinary thread spawn demands a static closure because a detached thread can outlive your stack. Switch to thread scope, and the compiler proves every worker joins before the scope returns — letting four threads mutate disjoint stack slices in place with zero Arc allocations and zero locks.

When threads coordinate, choose atomics with Acquire and Release for lock-free flags, or pass ownership through a bounded channel. Once full, the buffer pushes backpressure upstream; once every sender drops, the consumer drains and exits cleanly.

OS threads reserve roughly two MiB of stack each — wasteful for ten thousand idle sockets. Rust async allocates no stack at all. Calling an async function returns a lazy Future compiled into a tiny state machine enum. In our lab, a two-await pipeline compiles down to forty-eight bytes.

Nothing runs until an executor calls poll. If the socket is not ready, the future stores a Waker and returns Pending, freeing the thread immediately. When epoll or kqueue fires, wake signals the executor to poll again until Ready — while Pin keeps self-references locked in memory.

scenes.title: Inside Tokio: work stealing, blocking, and cancellation

beats.say: Tokio pairs that OS reactor with a multi-threaded work-stealing runtime. Idle workers steal half of a busy neighbor's local queue in one batch. The biggest trap is blocking a worker thread with synchronous work, starving every task behind it. Offload blocking calls with spawn blocking, or CPU parallelism with Rayon.

For structured lifecycles, a JoinSet aborts unfinished tasks on drop, while a Semaphore caps in-flight concurrency. And when select races a timeout against an RPC, cancellation is not an exception — Rust simply drops the losing Future, running every destructor automatically.

Put it all together in a real service: async ingesters gated by a Semaphore feed owned batches through a bounded mpsc channel to an actor that owns its state with zero mutexes, answering queries over oneshot and draining cleanly on a CancellationToken. Ownership is not bolted onto Rust concurrency. Ownership is Rust's concurrency model.
